cards.headline: A song teased in 1988 took 13 years to appear
cards.snippet: Leonard Cohen revealed in 1988 that he was working on a new song called 'My Secret Life'. It took until 2001 for it to reach record, on his album Ten New Songs. He wrote it with Sharon Robinson, who also played keyboards and programmed the drums and bass. Bob Metzger played electric guitar. That is a gap of 13 years between the first mention and the release.
cards.context: Ten New Songs, 2001; Robinson also played keyboards and programmed drums and bass.

cards.headline: The video was shot at Montreal's Habitat 67
cards.snippet: The music video for "In My Secret Life" was filmed in Montreal, Cohen's hometown, at Habitat 67. The building is known for its futuristic architecture. Moshe Safdie, a Jewish architect, designed it as his McGill University thesis, and it became tied to Expo 67 in 1967.
cards.context: Cohen's hometown; a commenter praises the surreal video and the brutalist setting.

cards.headline: The song as permission to stop running
cards.snippet: Leonard made me realise instead of running away from my misery it is ok to just sit with all of it and make peace with it.
cards.context: A listener describes the song's emotional effect.

cards.headline: Katie Melua's band-and-strings take, arranged by Mike Batt
cards.snippet: Katie Melua sings it with a full band and orchestra: Mike Batt produced, arranged and plays organ and piano, with four guitarists, Henry Spinetti on drums, Ray Cooper on percussion, plus strings, flute and brass.
cards.context: Melua named Cohen as her ideal songwriter in a 2004 Guardian item.
